gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari keeps its letter mouths wide open and its middle zone tall, a modern sans with nothing to hide. Anek Devanagari then sits beneath Origami, whose single-stroke brush lines never vary in width and give the heading its odd, poured-lead weight.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-gujarati: Clean and approachable, Anek Gujarati lets its lowercase rise almost to the capitals while the c gapes wide beside Origami's constant-width pen line. That gap between brush-drawn heading and plain sans text is what the pair does best.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-malayalam: Anek Malayalam reads tightly, with capitals barely above the lowercase and curves whose tips stop short of touching. Origami's o, with sides and top equally thick, leads above it, and the text underneath would keep a long page moving without fuss.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-odia: Solder squeezed through a nozzle, that's Origami's look, a lowercase mass of strokes pulled at constant width. Anek Odia does the quieter job, with unlatched round letters and capitals just above lowercase, while the heading does the shouting.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-tamil: Origami looks like lead type poured in one pass, with no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet. And Anek Tamil, with big round bowls and c and s forms that seem half unwrapped, would read easily across a long stretch.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-telugu: Glass-tube lettering, hollow and constant in thickness, is what Origami is about. Anek Telugu follows with wide, tall bowls and unlatched rounds, and a slightly larger size for the body would let those bowls breathe beside the heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anuphan: Origami draws every stroke at constant width, like bent pipe, in a lowercase mass of poured lead. Anuphan sits below it with big round bowls and open curves, so shrinking the heading would drain its weight while a large body would crowd it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-arimo: Pen-plotter smooth and a little odd, Origami heads the pair with its brush-drawn single stroke. Arimo takes over below with a tall mean line and generous gaps in its rounded glyphs, a sans that lets the heading carry the character.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-armata: Single pen tip, one line, no fuss: that is Origami. Armata follows with spacious gaps between characters and lowercase filling most of its height, so a body size a notch above the heading's usual would feel natural.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-athiti: Origami looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to one line width, with a lowercase mass of poured lead. And Athiti, with see-through gaps in each s and a high mean line, would feel friendly and unhurried over a long page.
